title: China Backs Southeast Asia Against US Unilateralism
text:
As global trade tensions rise, the relationship between China and malaysia is becoming increasingly vital.This article explores the strengthening ties between these two nations,notably in the context of US tariff policies and the evolving geopolitical landscape. Discover how Malaysia is navigating this complex environment and the implications of its growing partnership with China.
China and Malaysia Forge Stronger Ties Amid Global Trade Tensions President Xi Jinping’s visit underscores a united front against protectionism as Malaysia navigates complex geopolitical landscape.
Published: April 17,2024
Xi Jinping’s Pledge: A United Front Against Unilateralism President xi Jinping,during his state visit too Malaysia,voiced a commitment to collaborate wiht Malaysia and the broader Southeast Asian region to resist unilateralism and protectionism. This statement, made at a welcome dinner on April 16, is widely interpreted as a subtle critique of U.S. trade policies under former President Donald Trump.
Xi emphasized the importance of regional unity , stating that China and Malaysia will stand together with regional countries to counter the tide of geopolitical rivalry and bloc-based confrontation, as well as the backlash of unilateralism and protectionism.
Anwar Ibrahim Echoes China’s Sentiment Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim aligned with Xi’s outlook, lauding China’s outward-looking approach. He contrasted this with what he characterized as inward-focused rivalry observed elsewhere on the global stage.
In some quarters, the rules-based order has been turned on its head – dialog has yielded to demands, tariffs are imposed without restraint, and the language of cooperation is drowned out by threats and coercion.
Anwar ibrahim, Prime Minister of Malaysia
anwar further elaborated on the implications of these shifts in global trade dynamics.
What we are witnessing today is not an honest reckoning with the imperfections of globalisation,but a retreat into economic tribalism.Market access is being weaponised. What was once a multilateral covenant for shared growth now buckles under the weight of arbitrary disruption and unilateral whim.
Anwar Ibrahim,Prime Minister of Malaysia
He affirmed China as a rational,strong,and reliable partner amidst the uncertainty caused by U.S. tariffs.
Background: US-China Trade tensions Xi’s visit occurred shortly after the U.S. announced a 90-day pause on reciprocal tariffs, while simultaneously increasing tariffs on Chinese imports.This move followed a period where several Southeast Asian economies faced significant tariffs from the U.S., including Cambodia (49%), Vietnam (46%), and Malaysia (24%).
Key Trade Figures China has been Malaysia’s largest trading partner since 2009. Bilateral trade reached RM484.12 billion (S$144.5 billion) in 2024, accounting for 16.8% of Malaysia’s total global trade. ASEAN ‘s trade with China totaled US$980 billion (S$1.28 trillion) in 2024. China and ASEAN have been each other’s top trading partners since 2020. Malaysia’s Position: Asean centrality As the current chair of ASEAN, Malaysia is committed to promoting free trade and maintaining ASEAN centrality amid rising geopolitical tensions.Anwar Ibrahim emphasized Malaysia’s self-reliant stance in a joint interview.
We should not, and do not need to, be constrained by any side. So far, we have refused to succumb to such pressure. Our position is clear: we cooperate with those who treat us with respect.
Anwar Ibrahim, Prime Minister of Malaysia
He also highlighted Malaysia’s positive relationship with China, stating, Although China is a major power with a strong economy and formidable military strength, we have never felt any sense of trouble or pressure from it.
Expert Analysis: Shifting Alliances? Dr. Lam Choong Wah, a senior lecturer from the University of Malaya, suggests that Anwar’s speech indicates the challenges the U.S. faces in isolating China from its regional neighbors.
The US-initiated tariff war hasn’t won the allies it hoped for – instead, it has alienated others. Malaysia, which has long maintained a neutral stance and pursued a hedging foreign policy, is now leaning towards China.
Dr. Lam Choong Wah, University of Malaya
However, Dr. Lam cautioned that closer ties with Beijing could increase the risk of reciprocal tariffs. He also noted the meaning of the 31 memorandums of understanding signed between Malaysia and China,covering various areas of cooperation.
Dr. Lam added, Essentially, Malaysia is moving into China’s orbit. It’s a non-binding but near-ally type partnership.
Asean Centrality: A Balancing Act mr. Lee Chean Chung, chairman of the Center of Regional Strategic Studies, emphasized malaysia’s commitment to ASEAN centrality by engaging with both Washington and Beijing.
Malaysia remains committed to the principle of regional autonomy, which lies at the heart of Asean’s mission as a regional alliance.
Mr. Lee Chean Chung, Centre of Regional Strategic Studies
The concept of ASEAN centrality underscores the region’s desire to shape its own future, rather than being dictated by external powers.
